canada.title: Canadian military flying ace William Barker commemorated with new statue on Yonge Street
canada.summary: A new statue of a Canadian World War I flying ace was unveiled in Toronto Wednesday afternoon, the latest effort to breathe life into his memory, which his grandson said was nearly lost to time.

canada.title: LifeLabs in B.C. ordered to pay $32K for misgendering transgender, non-binary patients: Human Rights Tribunal
canada.summary: B.C.'s Human Rights Tribunal has ordered LifeLabs and a subsidiary to pay three transgender and non-binary people $32,000 for "injury to their dignity" after the staff at the company misgendered and outed them at service centres in Vancouver and Burnaby in 2019.

canada.title: Community fundraising to bring CT scanner to Parkland County hospital
canada.summary: Parkland County residents are raising money for a CT scanner at the local hospital, to spare patients and families the stress of transfers. They aim to collect just over $5 million to bring the specialized imaging machine to the WestView Hospital and Continuing Care Centre in Stony Plain, Alta.

canada.title: Boys' competitive gymnastics program back in the Yukon after 15 years
canada.summary: It wasn’t lack of desire or interest that kept a boys' gymnastics program dormant for so many years in the Yukon — it was finding the right coach.

canada.title: Cuba-U.S. tensions force Canadians to consider pricier sun destinations: travel agents
canada.summary: As the winter holiday season approaches, one of the most popular sunny destinations for Canadian travellers remains out of reach.

canada.title: Is the Alberta government engaging in American-style gerrymandering?
canada.summary: Political science experts told CBC’s West of Centre that Alberta’s electoral map-making process should be reexamined to stave off American influences.

canada.title: These Sask. sisters had mastectomies on the same day. Only 1 of them had cancer
canada.summary: Sisters Lila and Julia McCormick both had mastectomies on Sept. 9. One was for cancer treatment, the other for prevention.

canada.title: Seven officers fired, a force under scrutiny: Can Montreal police rebuild public trust?
canada.summary: Seven officers have been fired amid a sweeping misconduct scandal. Critics question if firings and transparency are enough for Montreal police to deliver accountability.

canada.title: Avalanche search dog associations warn of public safety risk after Parks Canada cuts Banff K9 program
canada.summary: The Canadian Avalanche Rescue Dog Association and British Columbia Search Dog Association have asked Parks Canada to “immediately reverse” the program’s cancellation to “reduce risks to rescuers and the Canadian public.”

canada.title: Not his first rodeo: Seasoned Sask. cowboy competitor mentors next generation
canada.summary: Scott Sigfusson started competing in rodeos at a young age. While the Tugaske, Sask., cowboy is not stopping anytime soon, he has turned more of his attention toward mentoring the next generation of cowboys and cowgirls.

canada.title: Farmers pleased with federal budget's proposed changes allowing land to be given to nieces, nephews tax-free
canada.summary: Expanded tax rollover rules in the 2026 federal budget are set to allow Canadian farm families to pass land down to nieces and nephews tax-free, a move producers and industry experts call a game-changer for preserving family operations.

canada.title: Young southeast Manitobans step into the line dancing scene
canada.summary: Friends Ava Kroeker and Aleah Kamerman started Silver Line Dancing in hopes of bringing line dancing to more young people in southeast Manitoba.

canada.title: New Brunswick's giant duck 'out in the middle of nowhere'
canada.summary: Deep in the woods, a giant duck made of rock presides over about two dozen small rock ducks and several genuine rubber ducks. The flock delights the many who travel by offroad vehicle toward the remote home of Brad and Lorrie Swan, the couple who started it all.

canada.title: Quispamsis Para cyclist Alexandre Hayward wins elimination race bronze at world championships
canada.summary: Quispamsis Para cyclist Alex Hayward won bronze in the elimination race at the Para-Cycling Track World Championships, edged by New Zealand in a three-rider sprint. Parasport NB says his success inspires young athletes and hopes to see him at the 2028 Paralympics.

canada.title: New grid operator says it will take over control from Nova Scotia Power in 2028
canada.summary: The new entity tasked with managing Nova Scotia’s electricity grid in the interest of ratepayers says it will take the reins away from Nova Scotia Power in the spring of 2028.

canada.title: After a wave of 'unheard of' closures, N.S. craft brewers see signs of stability
canada.summary: After an "unheard of" wave of brewery closures earlier this year, the president of Nova Scotia's craft brewers association says the industry has finally stabilized.

canada.title: Looking for a career in mining? Future geologists get to tap into the industry at conference
canada.summary: Delegates from the mining industry are in St. John's this week for the Mineral Resources Review conference. But they're not the only ones in attendance —students from O'Donel High School were there to learn about careers in mining.

canada.title: In a city of multi-hyphenate artists, actor-writer-director Zoe Cleland finds community
canada.summary: As an actor-writer-director, Zoe Cleland appreciates the “bubbling creativity” in the St. John's artistic community, a place full of multi-hyphenate individuals working on diverse projects and supporting each other’s efforts.
